\chapter{Nothing, Not Yet, That Will Do}
\label{ch:te-nothing-not-yet}
\hlchaptermodality{98}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can answer with nothing, not yet, that will do, that's true, and that's the one.}

Complete TE-C98-thatone: five short answers that close a question.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[ēmī lēdu]{\te{ఏమీ} \te{లేదు} (ēmī lēdu) — nothing, it's nothing}

\label{lesson:TE-C98-nothing}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for worry, then the Telugu for alone.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{ఏమీ} \te{లేదు}}
\textbf{\te{ఏమీ} \te{లేదు}} (\emph{ēmī lēdu}) — \textquotedblleft{}nothing\textquotedblright{}, \textquotedblleft{}it's nothing\textquotedblright{}.

The answer to \textbf{\te{ఏమైంది}?}, \textquotedblleft{}what happened?\textquotedblright{}, when you would rather not say. It ends on the \textbf{\te{లేదు}} you have had since your first chapter.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
An answer that closes a question kindly.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ēmī lēdu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ēmī lēdu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{ēmī lēdu}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for worry, then the Telugu for alone, then say \emph{ēmī lēdu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{ఏమీ} \te{లేదు} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Nothing, it's nothing\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[iṅkā lēdu]{\te{ఇంకా} \te{లేదు} (iṅkā lēdu) — not yet}

\label{lesson:TE-C98-notyet}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for alone, then the Telugu for nothing.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{ఇంకా} \te{లేదు}}
\textbf{\te{ఇంకా} \te{లేదు}} (\emph{iṅkā lēdu}) — \textquotedblleft{}not yet\textquotedblright{}.

Two words you own, \textbf{\te{ఇంకా}}, \textquotedblleft{}still\textquotedblright{}, and \textbf{\te{లేదు}}, \textquotedblleft{}there isn't\textquotedblright{}. \emph{Have you eaten?} — \textbf{\te{ఇంకా} \te{లేదు}}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
An answer from two old words.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iṅkā lēdu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iṅkā lēdu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} answer \emph{bhōñcēśārā?} with \emph{iṅkā lēdu}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for alone, then the Telugu for nothing, then say \emph{iṅkā lēdu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{ఇంకా} \te{లేదు} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Not yet\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[saripōtundi]{\te{సరిపోతుంది} (saripōtundi) — that will do, it is enough}

\label{lesson:TE-C98-enough}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for nothing, then the Telugu for not yet.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{సరిపోతుంది}}
\textbf{\te{సరిపోతుంది}} (\emph{saripōtundi}) — \textquotedblleft{}that will do\textquotedblright{}, \textquotedblleft{}it is enough\textquotedblright{}, and of clothes, \textquotedblleft{}it fits\textquotedblright{}.

It starts on \textbf{\te{సరి}}, \textquotedblleft{}right, even\textquotedblright{}, like \textbf{\te{సరే}} and \textbf{\te{సరిగ్గా}}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A third word on the same right-even root.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{saripōtundi}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{saripōtundi}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{saripōtundi}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for nothing, then the Telugu for not yet, then say \emph{saripōtundi} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{సరిపోతుంది} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}That will do, it is enough\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[nijamē]{\te{నిజమే} (nijamē) — that's true}

\label{lesson:TE-C98-true}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for not yet, then the Telugu for that will do.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{నిజమే}}
\textbf{\te{నిజమే}} (\emph{nijamē}) — \textquotedblleft{}that's true\textquotedblright{}, \textquotedblleft{}quite right\textquotedblright{}.

It is \textbf{\te{నిజం}} with \textbf{-\te{ఏ}}, the ending that says \emph{exactly this}. Where \textbf{\te{నిజంగా}?} asks, \textbf{\te{నిజమే}} agrees.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Agreement, from the word for truth.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nijamē}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nijamē}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{nijamē}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for not yet, then the Telugu for that will do, then say \emph{nijamē} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{నిజమే} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}That's true\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[adē]{\te{అదే} (adē) — that's the one, the same}

\label{lesson:TE-C98-thatone}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for that will do, then the Telugu for that's true.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{అదే}}
\textbf{\te{అదే}} (\emph{adē}) — \textquotedblleft{}that's the one\textquotedblright{}, \textquotedblleft{}the same one\textquotedblright{}.

It is \textbf{\te{అది}}, \textquotedblleft{}that\textquotedblright{}, with the same \textbf{-\te{ఏ}}. When someone finally names what you meant, \textbf{\te{అదే}!}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Nothing, not yet, that will do, true, that's the one: five ways to close a question.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{adē}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{adē}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{adē!}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for that will do, then the Telugu for that's true, then say \emph{adē} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{అదే} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}That's the one, the same\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
